paragraphs.name: FILE-CONTROL
paragraphs.narrative: This section defines all the input and output files used by the program. It specifies the physical characteristics of each file, such as the record format, block size, and organization (sequential, indexed, etc.). It also links the file names used within the COBOL program to the actual physical file names on the system. This allows the program to access and manipulate the data stored in these files. Without this section, the program would not know how to interact with the external data sources and destinations.
paragraphs.purpose: To declare and configure the files the program will read from and write to.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the main control loop for the program. It first performs the initialization routine to set up the program environment. Then, it repeatedly finds the next authorization summary record and processes it until there are no more summary records to process. After processing all summary records, the program performs final cleanup tasks and terminates. This paragraph orchestrates the overall flow of the program, ensuring that each step is executed in the correct order.
paragraphs.purpose: To manage the main processing loop of the program, driving the overall authorization purging process.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed at the beginning of the program to set up initial values for key variables and flags. It opens the necessary input and output files, preparing them for processing. It also initializes counters and status indicators that will be used throughout the program to track progress and handle errors. This ensures that the program starts in a known and consistent state, preventing unexpected behavior due to uninitialized data.
paragraphs.purpose: To prepare the program for execution by setting up initial values and opening files.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph provides a single point of exit from the initialization routine. It ensures that all initialization steps have been completed before proceeding to the main processing logic. It is a standard COBOL practice to have a dedicated exit paragraph for each routine to improve code readability and maintainability. This paragraph does not perform any specific actions other than providing a controlled exit point.
paragraphs.purpose: To provide a controlled exit point from the initialization routine.

paragraphs.name: 2000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-SUMMARY
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph reads the next authorization summary record from the input file. It checks if the end of the file has been reached. If the end of the file is reached, it sets a flag to indicate that there are no more summary records to process. Otherwise, it makes the data from the summary record available for further processing. This paragraph is responsible for iterating through the authorization summary records.
paragraphs.purpose: To retrieve the next authorization summary record for processing.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph provides a single point of exit from the summary record retrieval routine. It ensures that the program returns to the calling paragraph after attempting to read a summary record, regardless of whether a record was successfully read or the end of the file was reached. This paragraph does not perform any specific actions other than providing a controlled exit point.
paragraphs.purpose: To provide a controlled exit point from the summary record retrieval routine.

paragraphs.name: 3000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-DTL
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph reads the next authorization detail record associated with the current summary record. It checks if the end of the detail records for the current summary has been reached. If the end is reached, it sets a flag to indicate that there are no more detail records for the current summary. Otherwise, it makes the data from the detail record available for further processing. This paragraph is responsible for iterating through the authorization detail records for each summary record.
paragraphs.purpose: To retrieve the next authorization detail record associated with the current summary record.

paragraphs.name: 3000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph provides a single point of exit from the detail record retrieval routine. It ensures that the program returns to the calling paragraph after attempting to read a detail record, regardless of whether a record was successfully read or the end of the detail records for the current summary was reached. This paragraph does not perform any specific actions other than providing a controlled exit point.
paragraphs.purpose: To provide a controlled exit point from the detail record retrieval routine.

paragraphs.name: 4000-CHECK-IF-EXPIRED
paragraphs.business_name: Determine if Authorization Detail is Expired
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph determines if the current authorization detail record has expired. It compares the expiration date of the authorization detail record against the current date or a predefined expiration policy. If the authorization detail record is expired, it sets a flag to indicate that it should be deleted. The logic within this paragraph implements the business rules for determining when an authorization is considered expired.
paragraphs.purpose: To evaluate whether an authorization detail record has expired based on predefined criteria.

paragraphs.name: 4000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph provides a single point of exit from the expiration check routine. It ensures that the program returns to the calling paragraph after checking if the authorization detail record is expired. This paragraph does not perform any specific actions other than providing a controlled exit point.
paragraphs.purpose: To provide a controlled exit point from the expiration check routine.

paragraphs.name: 5000-DELETE-AUTH-DTL
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed when the program determines that an authorization detail record needs to be deleted. It physically removes the authorization detail record from the system's database. The paragraph reads the specific authorization detail record identified for deletion. After the deletion, the paragraph updates any necessary counters or flags to reflect the removal of the record.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles the physical deletion of an expired authorization detail record from the system.

paragraphs.name: 5000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Delete Authorization Detail Record' process. It ensures a clean exit from the deletion routine. Control is returned to the calling paragraph, typically after a successful deletion or if a deletion was not required. No data manipulation or processing occurs within this paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a controlled exit point from the authorization detail deletion process.

paragraphs.name: 6000-DELETE-AUTH-SUMMARY
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is triggered when all associated detail records for a given authorization summary record have been deleted. It removes the authorization summary record from the system's database. The paragraph reads the specific authorization summary record identified for deletion. After the deletion, the paragraph updates any necessary counters or flags to reflect the removal of the record.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles the deletion of an authorization summary record when all its detail records have been purged.

paragraphs.name: 6000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Delete Authorization Summary Record' process. It ensures a clean exit from the summary deletion routine. Control is returned to the calling paragraph, typically after a successful deletion or if a deletion was not required. No data manipulation or processing occurs within this paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a controlled exit point from the authorization summary deletion process.

paragraphs.name: 9000-TAKE-CHECKPOINT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is called periodically to create a checkpoint during the authorization purging process. It saves the current state of the program, including the last processed record and any relevant counters, to a checkpoint file or database. This allows the program to be restarted from this point in case of a failure. The checkpoint data is written to a designated storage location. After writing the checkpoint, the program continues with the next authorization record.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph ensures that the program can be restarted from a known point in case of failure, preventing data loss and reprocessing.

paragraphs.name: 9000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Take Checkpoint' process. It ensures a clean exit from the checkpoint routine. Control is returned to the calling paragraph, typically after a successful checkpoint was taken. No data manipulation or processing occurs within this paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a controlled exit point from the checkpoint process.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is invoked when a critical error occurs that prevents the program from continuing its normal execution. It performs necessary cleanup actions, such as closing files and releasing resources. An error message is written to the system log, indicating the reason for the abnormal termination. The program then terminates with an error code, signaling to the operating system that an error occurred.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles abnormal program termination due to errors, ensuring proper cleanup and error reporting.

paragraphs.name: 9999-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Abnormal Termination' process. It ensures a clean exit from the abend routine. Control is returned to the operating system. No data manipulation or processing occurs within this paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a controlled exit point from the abnormal termination process.

business_purpose: This batch program, CBPAUP0C, is responsible for purging expired authorization data from the system. It iterates through authorization summary records and, for each summary, it examines the associated detail records. The program checks if the authorization has expired based on a predefined expiration policy. If an authorization detail record is expired, it is deleted. If all detail records for a given summary record are deleted due to expiration, the summary record itself is also deleted. The program takes checkpoints periodically to ensure that the process can be restarted from the last successful point in case of failure. The copybooks CIPAUDTY and CIPAUSMY are used to define the data structures for authorization detail and summary records, respectively.
complexity_reason: The program's logic is straightforward, but the lack of explicit file/database access information requires further investigation to understand the underlying data storage and access mechanisms.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job
migration_approach: 1. Analyze the copybooks CIPAUDTY and CIPAUSMY to fully understand the structure of the authorization detail and summary records and how they are stored (e.g., VSAM files, DB2 tables).
2. Identify the underlying data storage mechanism and migrate the data to a modern database (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL).
3. Re-implement the COBOL logic in a modern language (e.g., Java, Python) using a scheduling framework (e.g., Spring Batch, Apache Airflow) to execute the purge process periodically.
4. Implement appropriate logging and monitoring to track the execution of the batch job and identify any errors.
5. Implement robust error handling and restart capabilities, mirroring the checkpoint functionality of the original COBOL program.
data_contracts: Input: Authorization summary and detail records. Output: Deletion of expired authorization detail and summary records.
migration_risks: Potential data integrity issues during migration, performance bottlenecks in the modern implementation, and ensuring accurate replication of the expiration policy.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the main control loop for the authorization processing. It continuously performs the main processing steps until a condition to stop is met. The loop involves receiving a request, processing the request, and sending a response. The specific logic for processing and the exit condition are handled in other paragraphs. This paragraph ensures continuous operation of the authorization process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph orchestrates the continuous processing of authorization requests.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph initializes the program by setting up initial values and states. It prepares the program for processing authorization requests. This includes setting up variables, opening necessary files or connections, and performing any other setup tasks. The paragraph ensures that the program starts in a known and consistent state. This is the first paragraph executed when the program starts.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph prepares the program for processing by setting up initial values and states.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph marks the end of the initialization process. It ensures a clean exit from the initialization routine. It may contain logic to handle any cleanup or finalization steps related to initialization. This paragraph is executed after the initialization steps are completed. It returns control to the calling paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph marks the end of the initialization process and returns control to the calling paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-REQUEST-QUEUE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph establishes a connection to the request queue. It prepares the program to receive authorization requests from the queue. The paragraph includes the necessary commands or functions to open the queue and make it available for reading messages. It handles any errors that may occur during the queue opening process. Successful execution of this paragraph is essential for the program to receive authorization requests.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph establishes a connection to the request queue, enabling the program to receive authorization requests.

paragraphs.name: 1100-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph handles the exit from the request queue opening process. It ensures a clean exit from the queue opening routine. It may contain logic to handle any cleanup or finalization steps related to opening the queue. This paragraph is executed after the queue opening steps are completed. It returns control to the calling paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph marks the end of the request queue opening process and returns control to the calling paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 1200-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as a generic exit point. It ensures a clean exit from a routine. It may contain logic to handle any cleanup or finalization steps. This paragraph is executed after the main steps are completed. It returns control to the calling paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a generic exit point for various routines, ensuring a clean return to the calling paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 2000-MAIN-PROCESS
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph orchestrates the main processing steps for an authorization request. It calls other paragraphs to extract the request message, validate the request, and send a response. It acts as a central control point for the authorization processing logic. The paragraph ensures that each request is processed according to the defined business rules. It handles any errors that may occur during the processing steps.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph orchestrates the main processing steps for an authorization request, including extraction, validation, and response sending.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph marks the end of the main processing routine. It ensures a clean exit from the main processing logic. It may contain logic to handle any cleanup or finalization steps related to the main processing. This paragraph is executed after the main processing steps are completed. It returns control to the calling paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph marks the end of the main processing routine and returns control to the calling paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 2100-EXTRACT-REQUEST-MSG
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph extracts the relevant information from the authorization request message. It parses the message and identifies the data elements needed for validation and processing. The extracted data is stored in working storage variables for subsequent use. The paragraph handles any errors that may occur during the message extraction process. This is a crucial step in preparing the request for validation.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph extracts the relevant information from the authorization request message, preparing it for validation and processing.

paragraphs.name: 2100-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph handles the exit from the request message extraction process. It ensures a clean exit from the extraction routine. It may contain logic to handle any cleanup or finalization steps related to extracting the message. This paragraph is executed after the extraction steps are completed. It returns control to the calling paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph marks the end of the request message extraction process and returns control to the calling paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 3100-READ-REQUEST-MQ
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is the main entry point for reading authorization requests. It continuously attempts to read a new authorization request from the message queue. If a request is successfully read, the data from the request is stored in a working storage area for further processing. If there are no requests available, the program waits until a new request arrives in the queue. After successfully reading a request, the program proceeds to process the authorization.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves the next authorization request from the message queue, making it available for processing.

paragraphs.name: 3100-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Read Authorization Request from Queue' process. It ensures a clean exit from the read operation. No specific actions are performed other than providing a single point of exit. Control returns to the calling paragraph, which would typically be the main processing loop.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the read request process.

paragraphs.name: 5000-PROCESS-AUTH
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is triggered after an authorization request is successfully read from the queue. It extracts key data elements from the request, such as account number and transaction amount. The paragraph then initiates the process of validating the authorization request by calling other paragraphs to read cross-reference, account, and customer records. Based on the data retrieved from these records, the authorization request will be approved or denied. Finally, the paragraph prepares a response message indicating the authorization status.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph orchestrates the validation of the authorization request by retrieving related data and determining the approval status.

paragraphs.name: 5000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Process Authorization Request' process. It ensures a clean exit from the authorization processing. No specific actions are performed other than providing a single point of exit. Control returns to the calling paragraph, which would typically be the main processing loop to read the next request.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the authorization processing.

paragraphs.name: 5100-READ-XREF-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is called by the 'Process Authorization Request' paragraph to retrieve a cross-reference record. It uses data from the authorization request, such as a transaction code, to locate the corresponding cross-reference record. The cross-reference record contains information needed to validate the authorization, such as transaction limits or restrictions. If the record is not found, an error condition is set. The data from the cross-reference record is then used in subsequent validation steps.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves the cross-reference record needed for authorization validation based on the transaction code.

paragraphs.name: 5100-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Read Cross-Reference Record' process. It ensures a clean exit from the read operation. No specific actions are performed other than providing a single point of exit. Control returns to the calling paragraph, which is the 'Process Authorization Request' paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the cross-reference record retrieval.

paragraphs.name: 5200-READ-ACCT-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is called by the 'Process Authorization Request' paragraph to retrieve the account record associated with the authorization request. It uses the account number from the request to locate the corresponding account record. The account record contains information such as the account balance, status, and credit limit. If the record is not found, an error condition is set. The data from the account record is then used in subsequent validation steps.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves the account record needed for authorization validation based on the account number.

paragraphs.name: 5200-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Read Account Record' process. It ensures a clean exit from the read operation. No specific actions are performed other than providing a single point of exit. Control returns to the calling paragraph, which is the 'Process Authorization Request' paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the account record retrieval.

paragraphs.name: 5300-READ-CUST-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is called by the 'Process Authorization Request' paragraph to retrieve the customer record associated with the authorization request. It uses the customer number (likely obtained from the account record) to locate the corresponding customer record. The customer record contains information such as the customer's name, address, and other demographic data. If the record is not found, an error condition is set. The data from the customer record may be used for additional validation or reporting purposes.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves the customer record, potentially for additional validation or reporting, based on the customer number.

paragraphs.name: 5300-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the 'Read Customer Record' process. It ensures a clean exit from the read operation. No specific actions are performed other than providing a single point of exit. Control returns to the calling paragraph, which is the 'Process Authorization Request' paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the customer record retrieval.

business_purpose: This program processes authorization requests received from a message queue. It initializes by opening a connection to the request queue. The program then continuously reads authorization requests from the queue, extracts the relevant information, and validates the request against a cross-reference record. After processing, the program sends a response back to a different queue. Finally, it closes the connection to the request queue.
user_role: Another application or system component that needs authorization.
complexity_reason: The program's reliance on MQ series and the need to understand the message formats and queue interactions increases migration complexity.
modern_equivalent: Message queue consumer and producer, potentially integrated with a REST API for external interaction.
migration_approach: 1. Analyze MQ message formats for request and response to define data contracts.
2. Implement a message queue listener (e.g., using Kafka or AWS SQS) to receive authorization requests.
3. Translate COBOL business logic into a modern language (e.g., Java, Python, Go) to process the request and validate against the cross-reference record.
4. Implement a message queue producer to send the response back to the appropriate queue.
5. Create unit and integration tests to ensure the new service functions as expected.
data_contracts: Input: Authorization request message from MQ. Output: Authorization response message to MQ.
migration_risks: Accurate translation of COBOL business logic, ensuring message format compatibility, and maintaining performance parity.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the entry point for displaying authorization details. It first checks if the user is authorized to access this function. If authorized, it initializes the authorization data area and then proceeds to gather the authorization details based on the user's input. Finally, it populates the authorization list for display on the screen. If the user is not authorized, an error message is displayed.
paragraphs.purpose: This is the main control paragraph that orchestrates the display of authorization information.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed when the user presses the Enter key. It first validates the user's input from the screen. If the input is valid, it determines the action to be performed based on the input data. This might involve retrieving specific authorization details or navigating to a different screen. After processing the input, it updates the screen with the relevant information or redirects the user to the appropriate screen.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles user input entered via the Enter key, determining the next action based on that input.

paragraphs.name: GATHER-DETAILS
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves specific authorization details based on the user's selection. It uses the user's input to identify the relevant authorization record. Once the record is found, it extracts the necessary details, such as authorization level, effective date, and expiration date. These details are then formatted for display on the screen.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph fetches the detailed information for a selected authorization record.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PF7-KEY
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is triggered when the user presses the PF7 key, indicating a request to view the previous page of authorizations. It calculates the starting position for the previous page of data. It then retrieves the authorizations for that page and updates the screen display. If there are no previous pages, it may display a message indicating that the user is already on the first page.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph manages the navigation to the previous page of authorization records.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PF8-KEY
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is triggered when the user presses the PF8 key, indicating a request to view the next page of authorizations. It calculates the starting position for the next page of data. It then retrieves the authorizations for that page and updates the screen display. If there are no further pages, it may display a message indicating that the user is already on the last page.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph manages the navigation to the next page of authorization records.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD
paragraphs.business_name: Advance to Next Page of Authorizations
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph handles the logic for moving to the next page of authorization records. It determines if there are more authorizations to display. If there are, it updates the screen with the next set of authorizations. If not, it informs the user that they are at the end of the list. It also updates the internal pointers to keep track of the current position in the authorization list.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph updates the screen to display the next set of authorization records when the user requests to page forward.

paragraphs.name: GET-AUTHORIZATIONS
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves a set of authorization records from the data store. It uses the user's identification to filter the authorizations. It reads a specific number of authorizations, starting from a particular position in the data store. The retrieved authorizations are then stored in a work area for further processing.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph fetches a batch of authorization records based on the user's ID and current position in the list.

paragraphs.name: REPOSITION-AUTHORIZATIONS
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph adjusts the starting position within the authorization list. It's used when the user navigates forward or backward through the list. It calculates the new starting position based on the user's request and the total number of authorizations. It ensures that the starting position remains within the valid range of the authorization list.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph updates the internal pointers to reflect the user's navigation through the authorization list.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-AUTH-LIST
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph formats the retrieved authorization data for display on the user's screen. It takes the raw authorization data and converts it into a user-friendly format. This includes formatting dates, amounts, and descriptions. The formatted data is then moved to the screen output area, ready to be displayed to the user.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph prepares the authorization data for presentation on the screen.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-AUTH-DATA
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph initializes the work areas used to store authorization data. It clears out any previous data from these areas. It also sets initial values for counters and flags used in the authorization processing logic. This ensures that the program starts with a clean slate each time it's executed.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph sets up the necessary data structures for processing authorization information.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed when the user chooses to return to the previous screen. It first moves a specific return code into a field. Then, it moves a 'return' indicator into a screen field. Finally, it sends control back to the calling program, effectively navigating the user back to where they were before viewing the authorization details. No data is read or updated in this process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles the user's request to go back to the previous screen.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PAULST-SCREEN
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is responsible for displaying the authorization list screen to the user. It formats the data to be displayed on the screen, including authorization details and any relevant messages. It then sends the formatted screen data to the user's terminal. This allows the user to view the list of authorizations and related information. No data is read or updated in this process, it only displays data.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph displays the formatted authorization list to the user on their screen.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-PAULST-SCREEN
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed when the user interacts with the authorization list screen. It receives input from the user's screen, such as navigation commands (page forward, page backward) or a selection of a specific authorization. The received input is then stored in program variables for further processing. This allows the program to respond to the user's actions on the screen. No data is read or updated in this process, it only receives data.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph captures user input from the authorization list screen, such as navigation commands.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph populates the header section of the screen with relevant information. It retrieves data such as the current date, time, user ID, and any other contextual information to be displayed in the header. It then formats this information and moves it into the corresponding fields on the screen layout. This ensures that the user has the necessary context while viewing the authorization details. No data is read or updated in this process, it only formats and moves data.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph populates the screen header with relevant contextual information for the user.

paragraphs.name: GATHER-ACCOUNT-DETAILS
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves and formats account details for display on the screen. It starts by reading the account number from the screen input. It then uses this account number to retrieve related information, such as account type, status, and balance, from various data sources. The retrieved data is then formatted and moved into the corresponding fields on the screen layout. This provides the user with a comprehensive view of the account associated with the authorization.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves and formats account details based on the account number received from the screen.

paragraphs.name: GETCARDXREF-BYACCT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves card cross-reference information based on the account number. It uses the account number as input to query a card cross-reference file or database. If a matching record is found, it extracts relevant card details, such as card number and card type. This information is then used to further enrich the authorization details displayed to the user. If no matching record is found, it sets an indicator to signify that the card information is unavailable.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves card details associated with the account number from a cross-reference file.

paragraphs.name: GETACCTDATA-BYACCT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves detailed account data based on the account number. It uses the account number as input to query the account master file or database. If a matching record is found, it extracts various account attributes, such as account balance, credit limit, and interest rate. This information is then used to populate the screen with comprehensive account details. If no matching record is found, it sets an error indicator.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves detailed account information from the account master file using the account number.

paragraphs.name: GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves customer data based on the customer number associated with the account. It uses the customer number as input to query the customer master file or database. If a matching record is found, it extracts customer details, such as name, address, and contact information. This information is then used to populate the screen with relevant customer details. If no matching record is found, it sets an error indicator.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves customer information from the customer master file using the customer number.

paragraphs.name: GET-AUTH-SUMMARY
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves a summary of authorizations associated with the account. It queries the authorization database or file using the account number. It then aggregates the authorization data to create a summary, including the total number of authorizations, the total authorized amount, and the average authorization amount. This summary is then displayed on the screen to provide the user with an overview of the authorization activity. If no authorizations are found, a message indicating this is displayed.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves and summarizes authorization data for the account to provide an overview to the user.

paragraphs.name: SCHEDULE-PSB
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph prepares the program to access IMS databases by scheduling a Program Specification Block (PSB). It loads the PSB, which defines the program's access rights and data structures for interacting with the IMS database. It then checks for any errors during the scheduling process. If errors are detected, it sets an error indicator and potentially terminates the program. This step is crucial for ensuring the program can correctly access and manipulate data within the IMS environment.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph schedules the PSB to enable the program to access IMS databases.

business_purpose: This online program displays a list of authorizations to a user. It's triggered when a user wants to view authorization details. The program receives input from a screen, retrieves authorization data, formats it for display, and sends it back to the user's screen. The user can navigate through the list of authorizations using page forward and page backward functions. The program also allows the user to return to the previous screen.
complexity_reason: The program is online, but relatively simple with no file access, program calls, or CICS commands, suggesting a straightforward screen interaction.
modern_equivalent: REST API endpoint that retrieves and formats authorization data for display in a modern UI.
migration_approach: 1. Define a REST API endpoint for retrieving authorization data based on user input.
2. Create a service to fetch authorization data from the existing data source (if any, otherwise mock data).
3. Implement data transformation logic to format the data into a JSON structure suitable for the new UI.
4. Develop a modern UI component to display the authorization data retrieved from the API.

business_purpose: This batch program extracts authorization summary and detail records from a database and writes them to a GSAM (Generalized Sequential Access Method) file. The program reads authorization summary records, then for each summary record, it reads associated detail records. It then formats and writes these records to the GSAM file in a parent-child segment structure. The program uses external subroutines to perform the actual data insertion into the GSAM file. The purpose is likely to create a backup or extract of authorization data for reporting or archival purposes.
complexity_reason: The reliance on GSAM and unknown subroutines significantly increases complexity, requiring reverse engineering and potentially custom data transformation logic.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job or data pipeline that extracts data from the source database, transforms it, and loads it into a target data store.
migration_approach: 1. Analyze the unknown subroutines to understand their functionality and dependencies, documenting their purpose and data transformations.
2. Replace the GSAM file with a modern data store (e.g., relational database, NoSQL database, cloud storage) based on the data model and access patterns.
3. Extract data from the source database using modern data extraction tools or APIs.
4. Transform the extracted data to match the target data store schema, replicating the logic of the COBOL program and its subroutines.
5. Load the transformed data into the target data store using appropriate data loading tools or APIs, scheduling the job to run periodically.
data_contracts: Input: Authorization summary and detail records from a database. Output: Formatted authorization data in a parent-child segment structure written to a GSAM file (to be replaced with a modern data store).
migration_risks: Reverse engineering the unknown subroutines could be time-consuming and error-prone. Data transformation logic needs to be carefully implemented to ensure data integrity. GSAM replacement requires careful consideration of data access patterns and performance requirements.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the program's entry point and orchestrates the main processing steps. It first initializes the program environment by performing the '1000-INITIALIZE' paragraph. Then, it reads and processes root segment data from the input file by repeatedly performing an inline read and insert process. Next, it reads and processes child segment data from another input file, again using an inline read and insert process. Finally, it displays a completion message and terminates the program.
paragraphs.purpose: This is the main control paragraph that drives the entire data loading process.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph initializes the program by performing several setup tasks. It accepts the current date and time from the system. It then opens the root segment input file and the child segment input file for processing. If either file fails to open, an error message is displayed, and the program terminates. Finally, it displays a message indicating that the initialization is complete.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph prepares the program for processing by setting up the environment and opening necessary files.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the initialization process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a clean exit point for the initialization process.

paragraphs.name: 2000-READ-ROOT-SEG-FILE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph reads a record from the root segment input file. It checks if the end of the file has been reached. If the end of file is reached, it sets a flag to indicate that there are no more records to process. Otherwise, it populates the root segment data area with the data from the current record.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph reads root segment data from the input file for processing.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the root segment file reading process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a clean exit point for the root segment file reading process.

paragraphs.name: 2100-INSERT-ROOT-SEG
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph inserts a root segment into the database. It calls an external function (name unknown) to perform the database insertion, passing the root segment data. It then checks the return code from the database call. If the insertion is successful, it continues processing. If the insertion fails, it checks for specific error conditions and displays an appropriate error message.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph inserts the root segment data into the database.

paragraphs.name: 2100-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the root segment insertion process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a clean exit point for the root segment insertion process.

paragraphs.name: 3000-READ-CHILD-SEG-FILE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph reads a record from the child segment input file. It checks if the end of the file has been reached. If the end of file is reached, it sets a flag to indicate that there are no more child records to process. Otherwise, it populates the child segment data area with the data from the current record.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph reads child segment data from the input file for processing.

paragraphs.name: 3000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the child segment file reading process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a clean exit point for the child segment file reading process.

paragraphs.name: 3100-INSERT-CHILD-SEG
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph inserts a child segment into the database and links it to its parent root segment. It calls an external function (name unknown) to perform the database insertion, passing the child segment data. It then checks the return code from the database call. If the insertion is successful, it continues processing. If the insertion fails, it displays an error message.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph inserts the child segment data into the database and links it to the appropriate root segment.

paragraphs.name: 3100-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is reached at the end of the root segment processing logic. It serves as a clean exit point, ensuring that the program flow returns to the calling routine without performing any further actions. This paragraph is essential for maintaining structured programming practices. It does not read or write any data, nor does it make any decisions. It simply marks the end of the 3100 processing block.
paragraphs.purpose: Provides a standard exit point for the root segment processing logic.

paragraphs.name: 3200-INSERT-IMS-CALL
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is called to insert a root segment record into the database. It first prepares the data to be passed to the database insertion routine. Then, it calls an external function (UNKNOWN) to perform the actual database insertion. After the call, it checks the return code to determine if the insertion was successful. If the insertion fails, the program may execute error handling routines or retry the insertion based on the error code.
paragraphs.purpose: Handles the insertion of root segment data into the database.

paragraphs.name: 3200-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is reached at the end of the database insertion process. It acts as a clean exit point, ensuring that the program flow returns to the calling routine without performing any further actions. paragraphs.purpose: Provides a standard exit point for the database insertion logic.

paragraphs.name: 4000-FILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is called to close the input files used by the program. It first checks if the root segment input file is open. If it is, it closes the file. It then checks if the child segment input file is open, and if so, closes that file as well. If any errors occur during the closing process, an error message is displayed to the operator. This ensures that all files are properly closed before the program terminates.
paragraphs.purpose: Closes the input files to release resources and ensure data integrity.

business_purpose: This batch program loads authorization data into a database. It reads root segment data from an input file, and then inserts these root segments into the database. Subsequently, it reads child segment data from another input file and inserts these child segments, linking them to their respective root segments. The program also makes calls to external functions to interact with the database during the insertion process. Finally, the program closes the files and terminates.
complexity_reason: The program's database interaction through external calls and the need to maintain data integrity during the migration process increase complexity.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job
migration_approach: 1. Analyze the external database interaction functions to understand the database schema and operations.
2. Design a new database schema in the cloud environment, considering scalability and performance.
3. Develop a batch job using a modern language (e.g., Java, Python) to read data from the input files.
4. Implement the database insertion logic in the new batch job, ensuring data integrity and consistency.
5. Schedule the new batch job to run periodically, replacing the COBOL program.
data_contracts: The program consumes root and child segment data from input files and produces database records. The input files contain authorization data, and the output is the populated authorization database.
migration_risks: Data integrity during migration, performance of the new batch job, and compatibility of the new database schema with existing applications.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is the program's entry point and controls the main processing flow. It repeatedly performs an inline process to find and process authorization records. After processing all records, it performs another inline process to close files. Finally, the program terminates, returning control to the operating system.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph orchestrates the entire authorization data extraction and unloading process.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph initializes the program. It accepts the current date and time from the system. It then opens the input and output files. If either file fails to open, an error message is displayed. Finally, the program displays a startup message indicating the program has begun.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph prepares the program for processing by setting up the environment and opening necessary files.

paragraphs.name: 1000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the initialization process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the initialization logic.

paragraphs.name: 2000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-SUMMARY
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves the next authorization summary record. It first initializes a work area. Then, it calls an external program to read the next summary record. If the read is successful, it checks for specific conditions. If the conditions are met, it continues processing; otherwise, it skips to the end of the paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph reads authorization summary records from the input file.

paragraphs.name: 2000-EXIT
paragraphs.business_name: Find Next Authorization Summary Record Exit
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the authorization summary record retrieval process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the summary record retrieval logic.

paragraphs.name: 3000-FIND-NEXT-AUTH-DTL
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph retrieves the next authorization detail record associated with the current summary record. It first initializes a work area. Then, it calls an external program to read the next detail record. If the read is successful, it checks for specific conditions. If the conditions are met, it continues processing; otherwise, it skips to the end of the paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph reads authorization detail records from the input file.

paragraphs.name: 3000-EXIT
paragraphs.business_name: Find Next Authorization Detail Record Exit
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the authorization detail record retrieval process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the detail record retrieval logic.

paragraphs.name: 4000-FILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph closes the input and output files. Before closing each file, it checks if the file is open. If a file is open, it is closed. After closing the files, a message is displayed indicating the program has completed.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph closes the files used by the program, ensuring data integrity and releasing resources.

paragraphs.name: 4000-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph serves as the exit point for the file closing process.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the file closing logic.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph handles abnormal program termination. It moves an error code to a variable. It then displays an error message. Finally, the program terminates, returning control to the operating system.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a controlled exit point for the program when an unrecoverable error occurs.

paragraphs.name: 9999-EXIT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed when the program needs to exit. It serves as a clean exit point, ensuring that all processing is complete before the program terminates. No specific actions are performed within this paragraph; it simply marks the end of the program's execution path. Control is returned to the calling program or operating system. This paragraph ensures a controlled and predictable program termination.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides a standard exit point for the program.

business_purpose: This batch program extracts and unloads authorization data from two related data stores. It reads authorization summary records and, for each summary record, retrieves associated detail records. The program calculates date differences related to authorization expiry and potentially flags records based on these calculations. It then calls two external, unknown programs to process the summary and detail records. Finally, the program closes the files and produces a report of the number of records read, deleted, and written.
complexity_reason: The program's reliance on two unknown external programs introduces significant uncertainty and requires investigation to understand their functionality and dependencies.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job or data pipeline
migration_approach: 1. Analyze the 'UNKNOWN' programs to understand their functionality and dependencies. Document their inputs, outputs, and business logic.
2. Re-implement the COBOL logic in a modern language (e.g., Java, Python, Go) using appropriate data structures and algorithms.
3. Replace the file access with database queries or data stream processing, depending on the target architecture.
4. Implement the functionality of the 'UNKNOWN' programs as separate microservices or functions, ensuring they adhere to modern API standards.
5. Schedule the new batch job or data pipeline to run at the appropriate frequency, mirroring the original COBOL program's schedule.
data_contracts: Input: Authorization summary records and associated detail records. Output: Processed authorization data (format determined by the 'UNKNOWN' programs) and a report of record counts.
migration_risks: The 'UNKNOWN' programs represent a significant risk. Their functionality must be fully understood and accurately replicated. Data format conversions and potential data quality issues during migration are also risks.

paragraphs.name: 0001-OPEN-FILES
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is triggered at the start of the program. It opens the input transaction file for processing. If the file opening is unsuccessful, the program sets an error code. The program then exits, continuing to the next step if the file opens successfully, or terminating if the file open fails.

paragraphs.name: 1001-READ-NEXT-RECORDS
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is the main loop control. It repeatedly calls the 'Read Records' paragraph to fetch a transaction record. If a record is successfully read, it then calls the 'Treat Record' paragraph to process the record. This continues until the end of the input file is reached, at which point the program stops.
paragraphs.purpose: To control the reading and processing of each transaction record from the input file.

paragraphs.name: 1002-READ-RECORDS

If the end of the file is reached, a flag is set to indicate that there are no more records to process. The program then exits, returning control to the calling paragraph.

paragraphs.name: 1003-TREAT-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph receives a transaction record and determines the type of database operation to perform based on the record type code. It uses a case statement to evaluate the record type code. Depending on the code, it will branch to either insert, update, or delete the record in the database. After performing the appropriate action, the program exits.
paragraphs.purpose: To route the transaction record to the correct database operation based on its type.

paragraphs.name: 10031-INSERT-DB
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph inserts a new record into the DB2 database. It uses an embedded SQL INSERT statement to add the record. After the insert, it checks the SQL return code to determine if the insert was successful. If the insert fails, it sets an error code. The program then exits.

paragraphs.name: 10032-UPDATE-DB

After the update, it checks the SQL return code to determine if the update was successful. If the update fails, it sets an error code. The program then exits.
paragraphs.purpose: To modify an existing record in the DB2 database based on the transaction record data.

paragraphs.name: 10033-DELETE-DB

After the delete, it checks the SQL return code to determine if the delete was successful. If the delete fails, it sets an error code. The program then exits.

business_purpose: This program processes transaction records to update a DB2 database. The program handles errors by setting status codes and potentially terminating if a critical error occurs. The input records contain a record number and description, which are used in the database operations. The program is triggered by a batch scheduler.

business_purpose: This program processes messages related to account activities using IBM MQ. It opens connections to multiple MQ queues, retrieves messages from one or more input queues, processes the account information contained within those messages, and then sends updated or new messages to other output queues. The program handles opening, reading, writing, and closing of MQ queues. The specific account activities are determined by the content of the messages received.

2. Design equivalent message structures (e.g., JSON schema, Protobuf) for modern message queues.
3. Implement a message consumer in a modern language (e.g., Java, Python, Go) to read from the designated MQ input queue.
4. Translate the COBOL business logic into the new consumer, processing the message and performing the necessary account activities.
5. Implement message producers to send updated or new messages to the appropriate output queues using the new message format.

migration_risks: Message format discrepancies between COBOL and the new system, potential data loss during message transformation, and ensuring transactional consistency across the migration.

business_purpose: This program processes messages from a message queue. It opens several queues, retrieves messages from one queue, and then sends messages to other queues based on the content of the received message. The program interacts with a messaging system to receive, process, and route messages. It opens queues, gets messages, puts messages on other queues, and then closes the queues.

modern_equivalent: Message Queue Consumer/Producer
migration_approach: 1. Analyze the existing MQSeries configuration and message formats to understand the current message routing logic.
2. Select a cloud-native messaging service (e.g., AWS SQS, Azure Service Bus, Google Cloud Pub/Sub) that meets the application's requirements.
3. Refactor the COBOL program's logic into a modern programming language (e.g., Java, Python, Go) using the chosen cloud messaging service's SDK.
4. Implement message transformation logic to adapt the existing message formats to the new messaging system, if necessary.
5. Thoroughly test the migrated application to ensure message delivery, processing, and routing are functioning correctly.
data_contracts: The program consumes messages from a source queue and produces messages to multiple destination queues. The message content determines the routing logic.
migration_risks: Potential data loss during migration, incompatibility between the old and new messaging systems, and the complexity of replicating the existing message routing logic in the cloud.

business_purpose: This batch program processes transaction data to update account balances. It reads transaction records, retrieves corresponding account information, calculates interest and fees, and then updates the account balance. The program uses cross-reference files to link card numbers to account IDs. It also retrieves discount group information and interest rates to apply appropriate calculations before writing the updated transaction details.
complexity_reason: The program's batch nature, file access, and calculations involving interest and fees require careful consideration when migrating to a modern architecture.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job or event-driven microservice triggered by transaction data.
migration_approach: 1. Decompose the COBOL program into smaller, logical units based on functionality (e.g., transaction processing, interest calculation, balance update).
2. Design and develop corresponding microservices or functions for each unit, using a modern programming language and framework.
3. Migrate the data access logic to use a modern database system and ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) framework.
4. Implement a scheduler or event-driven mechanism to trigger the microservices based on the arrival of transaction data.
5. Thoroughly test the migrated components to ensure functional equivalence and performance.
data_contracts: Input: Transaction records, card cross-reference data, discount group information, interest rates. Output: Updated transaction details, updated account balances.
migration_risks: Ensuring data consistency during the migration, accurately replicating the interest and fee calculation logic, handling potential performance bottlenecks in the new architecture.

business_purpose: This batch program processes customer records. It opens a customer file, reads each record sequentially, and then closes the file. For each customer record, it extracts information such as customer ID, name, address, phone numbers, SSN, government-issued ID, date of birth, EFT account ID, primary cardholder indicator, and FICO credit score. The program also includes error handling routines for abnormal termination and displaying I/O status. It calls an external program named 'UNKNOWN' during the abnormal termination process.
complexity_reason: The program is relatively simple, involving sequential file processing and data extraction, but the 'UNKNOWN' program dependency needs investigation.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job or data pipeline task
migration_approach: 1. Analyze the 'UNKNOWN' program to understand its functionality and dependencies.
2. Re-implement the COBOL program logic in a modern language (e.g., Java, Python) using a data pipeline framework (e.g., Apache Beam, Apache Spark) or a scheduler.
3. Replace the sequential file access with access to a modern data store (e.g., cloud object storage, database).
4. Implement error handling and logging mechanisms equivalent to the COBOL program.
5. Deploy the new batch job or data pipeline to a cloud environment and schedule it to run at the appropriate frequency.
data_contracts: Input: Customer file (sequential). Output: Extracted customer data (potentially written to a database or another file).
migration_risks: The 'UNKNOWN' program's functionality is critical to understand. Data format differences between the mainframe file and the target data store could cause issues. Sensitive data (SSN, government ID) requires careful handling and encryption during migration.

After the files are open, it exports customer data, then account data, then cross-reference data, and finally transaction data. The program then terminates.

business_purpose: This batch program extracts customer, account, cross-reference, and transaction data from the legacy system and formats it into a standardized export file. The program is initiated by a scheduler. It opens several files, reads records from customer, account, cross-reference, and transaction files, transforms the data into a specific export record format, and writes these records to the export file. A timestamp is generated for each export run to ensure uniqueness and track when the data was extracted. The program calls an unknown external program.
complexity_reason: The program's complexity stems from its batch nature, data transformation logic, unknown external program dependency, and the need to maintain data integrity during the export process.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job or data pipeline
migration_approach: 1. Analyze the COBOL program to fully understand the data extraction, transformation, and export logic, paying close attention to the unknown external program's function.
2. Identify and document the data sources (customer, account, cross-reference, transaction files) and their corresponding schemas.

3. Develop a modern data pipeline using tools like Apache Spark, Apache Beam, or cloud-native data integration services (e.g., AWS Glue, Azure Data Factory, Google Cloud Dataflow) to replicate the COBOL program's functionality.
4. Implement the data transformation logic in the new pipeline, ensuring data type conversions and format compatibility with the target export file format.
5. Schedule the data pipeline to run at the same frequency as the original COBOL batch job, and thoroughly test the output data for accuracy and completeness.
data_contracts: The program consumes customer, account, cross-reference, and transaction data from legacy files. It produces a standardized export file containing records with customer, account, and transaction information, including a timestamp and sequence number.
migration_risks: Data integrity issues during transformation, performance bottlenecks in the new pipeline, compatibility issues with the target export file format, and the unknown functionality of the external program.

paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-PROCESSING
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is the entry point of the CBIMPORT program. It orchestrates the entire data import process by calling other paragraphs in a specific sequence. First, it initializes the program. Then, it processes the export file. After processing, it performs end-of-job processing. Finally, it terminates the program.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph controls the overall execution flow of the data import program.

paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph prepares the program for execution. It sets initial values for key variables, such as counters and flags, to ensure a clean start. It also moves values to working storage. The paragraph displays initial messages to the console or log file, providing information about the program's start-up process. Finally, it initializes the date.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph sets up the program environment before processing begins.

paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-FILES
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph opens all the necessary files for the program to function. It opens the input export file to read data from, and output files for writing processed data and error records. For each file, it checks if the open operation was successful. If a file fails to open, an error message is displayed, and a flag is set to indicate a file error. The program will terminate if any of the files cannot be opened.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph ensures that all required files are accessible before processing begins.

paragraphs.name: 2000-PROCESS-EXPORT-FILE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph controls the main processing loop for reading and processing records from the export file. It repeatedly reads records from the export file until the end of the file is reached. For each record read, it calls another paragraph to process the record based on its type. This continues until the end-of-file condition is met.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph drives the core logic of reading and processing each record from the input file.

paragraphs.name: 2100-READ-EXPORT-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph reads a single record from the export file. It attempts to read the next sequential record. If the end of the file is reached, it sets an end-of-file flag to signal that no more records are available. If the read is successful, the record is available for further processing.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph retrieves the next record from the input file for processing.

paragraphs.name: 2200-PROCESS-RECORD-BY-TYPE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph determines the type of record and calls the appropriate processing paragraph. It examines a record type code within the record. Based on the record type (Customer, Account, Cross-Reference, Transaction, or Card), it directs the processing to a specific paragraph designed to handle that record type. If the record type is invalid or unknown, no specific processing is performed.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph routes the processing of each record to the correct handler based on its type.

paragraphs.name: 2300-PROCESS-CUSTOMER-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph processes a customer record from the export file. It moves data from the export record to the corresponding fields in the customer record layout. It performs calculations, such as calculating an age based on the birthdate. If the customer record is valid, it writes the processed customer record to the customer file. If the record is invalid, it writes an error record to the error file.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles the specific logic for processing customer records.

paragraphs.name: 2400-PROCESS-ACCOUNT-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph processes an account record from the export file. It moves data from the export record to the corresponding fields in the account record layout. It performs calculations, such as calculating an average balance. If the account record is valid, it writes the processed account record to the account file. If the record is invalid, it writes an error record to the error file.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles the specific logic for processing account records.

paragraphs.name: 2500-PROCESS-XREF-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph processes a cross-reference record from the export file. It moves data from the export record to the corresponding fields in the cross-reference record layout. It performs calculations, such as calculating a relationship score. If the cross-reference record is valid, it writes the processed cross-reference record to the cross-reference file. If the record is invalid, it writes an error record to the error file.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles the specific logic for processing cross-reference records.

paragraphs.name: 2600-PROCESS-TRAN-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph processes a transaction record from the export file. It moves data from the export record to the corresponding fields in the transaction record layout. It performs calculations, such as calculating a transaction fee. If the transaction record is valid, it writes the processed transaction record to the transaction file. If the record is invalid, it writes an error record to the error file.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles the specific logic for processing transaction records.

paragraphs.name: 2650-PROCESS-CARD-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed when the import record type is 'Card'. It first initializes a work area to store the card record data. Then, it moves data from the import record into the card record work area. A calculation is performed to determine a derived value, which is also stored in the card record work area. Finally, the program writes the validated and processed card record to the card table. If the write operation is unsuccessful, an error flag is set.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph processes and stores card-related data from the import file into the banking system.

paragraphs.name: 2700-PROCESS-UNKNOWN-RECORD
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is triggered when the record type in the import file is not recognized. It moves the unknown record data into an error record work area. The paragraph then increments a counter for the number of unknown records encountered. Finally, it calls an inline routine to write the error record to the error file. This ensures that invalid or unexpected data is captured for later analysis.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles records with unrecognized types by writing them to an error file.

paragraphs.name: 2750-WRITE-ERROR
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is called to write an error record to the error file. It writes the error record from the error record work area to the error file. If the write operation fails, it checks if the error file is full. If the error file is not full, it increments a counter for the number of error records written. This ensures that all identified errors are logged for review.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph writes error records to the error file and tracks the number of errors encountered.

paragraphs.name: 3000-VALIDATE-IMPORT
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is used for basic validation during the import process. It displays messages to the console indicating the start and end of the validation process. These messages are primarily for monitoring the program's progress. No data validation or transformation occurs within this paragraph.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph provides basic monitoring of the import validation process.

paragraphs.name: 4000-FINALIZE
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed at the end of the program to perform cleanup tasks. It displays various status messages, including the number of records processed for each type (Customer, Account, Cross-Reference, Transaction, Card) and the number of errors encountered. It then closes all open files, including the import file, the customer file, the account file, the transaction file, the card file, and the error file. These actions ensure that all resources are released and the program terminates cleanly.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph closes files and displays summary information at the end of the program's execution.

paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.narrative: This paragraph is executed when a critical error occurs, causing the program to terminate prematurely. It calls an external routine (name unknown) to handle the abnormal termination process. It also displays an error message to the console, indicating that the program has terminated abnormally. This ensures that the system is notified of the failure and that appropriate actions can be taken.
paragraphs.purpose: This paragraph handles abnormal program termination due to critical errors.

business_purpose: This batch program, triggered by a scheduler, imports data from an external export file into the core banking system. It reads records from the export file, validates the data, and then processes each record based on its type (Customer, Account, Cross-Reference, Transaction, or Card). The program updates the corresponding customer, account, and transaction tables within the banking system. If a record type is unknown or invalid, the program writes an error record to an error file.
complexity_reason: The program's complexity stems from its batch nature, data validation logic, multiple record types, and database updates, requiring careful consideration of transaction management and data consistency in the cloud environment.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job or event-driven data ingestion pipeline.
suggested_service: Core banking service or data ingestion service.
migration_approach: 1. Extract the data validation and transformation logic into reusable functions or a dedicated data transformation service.
2. Implement a cloud-based scheduler (e.g., AWS Lambda triggered by CloudWatch Events, Azure Functions triggered by a timer) to initiate the data import process.
3. Develop a data ingestion pipeline using cloud-native services (e.g., AWS Kinesis, Azure Event Hubs, Google Cloud Pub/Sub) to handle the incoming data from the export file.
4. Implement data processing logic using serverless functions or containerized applications to process each record type and update the corresponding database tables.
5. Implement robust error handling and logging mechanisms to capture and report any errors during the data import process.
data_contracts: Input: External export file containing customer, account, cross-reference, transaction, and card data. Output: Updated customer, account, and transaction tables in the banking system, and an error file containing invalid records.
migration_risks: Data consistency issues during migration, potential performance bottlenecks with large export files, and ensuring data integrity during the transition to the cloud database.

It repeatedly performs several key operations: processing the cross-reference file, retrieving customer details, fetching account information, handling transaction records, and creating customer statements. Each of these operations is handled by a separate inline routine. After all records are processed, it closes the input files. This paragraph orchestrates the entire statement generation process.

business_purpose: This batch program generates monthly statements for customers. It starts by reading a cross-reference file to link card numbers to customer IDs. For each customer, it retrieves customer details and account information. Then, it processes transaction records, filters them, and formats them for inclusion in the statement. Finally, it creates an HTML statement file containing customer information and transaction details.
complexity_reason: The program's complexity stems from its batch nature, file processing, HTML generation, and unknown dependencies on numerous subprograms, requiring careful analysis and refactoring.
modern_equivalent: Scheduled batch job or a set of orchestrated microservices triggered by a scheduler.
migration_approach: 1. Analyze the called subprograms to understand their functionality and dependencies. Prioritize migrating these dependencies first.
2. Decompose the COBOL program into smaller, manageable microservices. One microservice could handle customer data retrieval, another for transaction processing, and another for statement generation.
3. Replace the file-based data access with database queries or calls to other microservices that manage the data.
4. Implement the transaction filtering and formatting logic in a modern programming language (e.g., Java, Python, Go).
5. Replace the HTML generation with a templating engine or a dedicated UI service that consumes data from the microservices.
data_contracts: Input: Cross-reference file (card number to customer ID), Customer details, Account information, Transaction records. Output: HTML statement file.
migration_risks: Unknown functionality of called subprograms, potential performance bottlenecks in transaction processing, ensuring data consistency during migration, complexity of HTML generation logic.
